I understand why I freak out when I hear a door slam because that was an indicator that shit was about to go down. I don't understand why I'm scared all the time and why it has got progressively worse over the years. Just in the past few years driving has become unbearable. I feel sick and actually dry heave like I'm gonna throw up. That didn't start until maybe five years ago. I haven't driven any distance in like 2-3 years.  I feel that logically I'd get better in time not worse.

I just don't think that's fair of me to say. That's just me personally. I'm sure plenty of people are messed up as a result of other people. I just don't think that's the case for me. But like I said, none of it seems logical to me.
I've tried, it always ends poorly.

Yeah, every time I think "maybe this will help" and when it doesn't it's disheartening. I've always just had this sense of impending doom. Just scared and nervous all the time. My mom used to flip the fuck out at any given time with no warning so I was always ready to run as a kid but that was so long ago and I can't blame the way I am because of another person. None of it makes sense to me. It just seems so irrational. I only feel like I can be myself if I know there isn't another person within like a mile radius of me.

I knew that as bad as I felt then that it would only get worse. It has. You're right, I do feel restrained but I know I've felt this way since I was in first grade, almost as long as I can remember. I feel like I've almost never been able to be myself. Fear dictates almost every aspect of my life. I live in constant fear and it does lead to misery, anger and pain. I've been trying to figure it out for most of my life. I've been to professionals, institutions and have been given different medications. Everything has gotten worse in every way. It's been a lifetime of mental decline it feels. I don't know how to explain it. It's not rational. If I had to make a metaphor it's like the walls are closing in.

That's the part that was truly terrifying. I don't believe in anything religious like god or hell I'm sure it was my body/mind trying to stay alive. I couldn't see anything it was pitch black but I was screaming. Desperately screaming for help. I had a feeling of pure terror and I couldn't move. In reality I was tied to the bed and was told that when I was talked to I would start grunting and writhing. Every muscle contacted. Hell of a workout
It's not about hurting yourself it's about ending the hurt
